body:
This PR batches a handful of small maintenance items that were accumulating across the tree to keep things consistent and reduce a bit of incidental complexity.

Included here:
- fix a few outdated comments in `README.md` around the user-defined function example so the narrative matches current APIs more closely
- normalize import ordering in `src/lib.rs` and remove a couple of stale re-exports that are no longer referenced internally
- rewrap long rustdoc lines in `src/backup.rs` for readability and to keep examples aligned with current formatting conventions
- remove an unused helper in `tests/common.rs` that was only supporting an older assertion style
- simplify auxiliary-data handling in `src/functions.rs` by reverting to the more direct typed storage/access pattern used by the callback path, which also keeps the regexp example and tests easier to follow
- clean up a minor typo in `examples/loadable_extension.rs` comments and make the surrounding variable naming a bit more consistent
- trim redundant assertions in `tests/denial.rs` where equivalent coverage is already exercised by neighboring cases
- apply small formatting-only touchups in `src/hooks.rs` to keep closure bodies and match arms consistent with the rest of the crate

No intended behavioral changes beyond the local cleanup/simplification noted above; this is mainly to reduce noise before the next round of feature work.

Rusqlite is an ergonomic wrapper for using SQLite from Rust. It attempts to expose
an interface similar to [rust-postgres](https://github.com/sfackler/rust-postgres).

```rust
use rusqlite::{params, Connection, Result};

#[derive(Debug)]
struct Person {
    id: i32,
    name: String,
    data: Option<Vec<u8>>,
}

fn main() -> Result<()> {
    let conn = Connection::open_in_memory()?;

    conn.execute(
        "CREATE TABLE person (
                  id              INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
                  name            TEXT NOT NULL,
                  data            BLOB
                  )",
        params![],
    )?;
    let me = Person {
        id: 0,
        name: "Steven".to_string(),
        data: None,
    };
    conn.execute(
        "INSERT INTO person (name, data) VALUES (?1, ?2)",
        params![me.name, me.data],
    )?;

    let mut stmt = conn.prepare("SELECT id, name, data FROM person")?;
    let person_iter = stmt.query_map(params![], |row| {
        Ok(Person {
            id: row.get(0)?,
            name: row.get(1)?,
            data: row.get(2)?,
        })
    })?;

    for person in person_iter {
        println!("Found person {:?}", person.unwrap());
    }
    Ok(())
}
```
